name: arrayfun
signature:
B = arrayfun(func, A)
B = arrayfun(func, A1, ..., An)
B = arrayfun(___, 'UniformOutput', false)
B = arrayfun(___, 'ErrorHandler', errorFunc)
[B1, ..., Bm] = arrayfun(___)
summary: A function applied to each element of one or more arrays (struct arrays too), the results in an array or a cell array.
differs: It refuses some inputs Octave accepts, e.g. arrayfun(@(x) 1:x, 'abc', 'UniformOutput', false).
It accepts some inputs Octave refuses: arrayfun(@(x) 1:x, true, 'UniformOutput', false) gives cell 1x1 {double 1x1 1}.
Found by a probe of edge values against GNU Octave 8.4.0 (scripts/catalog-probe-matlab.py; catalog/matlab/probes/octave.json).

name: cell
signature:
C = cell(n)
C = cell(sz1, ..., szN)
C = cell(sz)
summary: A cell array of empty double arrays, of a given size.
doc: Takes the same size arguments as `zeros`.

name: cellfun
signature:
A = cellfun(func, C)
A = cellfun(func, C1, ..., Cn)
A = cellfun(___, 'UniformOutput', false)
A = cellfun(___, 'ErrorHandler', errorFunc)
[A1, ..., Am] = cellfun(___)
summary: A function applied to each cell of one or more cell arrays, the results in an array, or in a cell array with 'UniformOutput' false.
doc: With uniform output each call must return a scalar; the results' class is theirs. `func` may also be one of the legacy names such as 'isempty' or 'length'.

name: isfield
summary: Whether a structure has a field, or which of several names are fields, as logical values.
doc: With a cell array of names, the result has one element per name. A non-structure gives false.

name: struct
signature:
s = struct
s = struct(field, value)
s = struct(field1, value1, ..., fieldN, valueN)
s = struct([])
summary: A structure, or a struct array when values are cell arrays: one element per cell, a scalar or one-cell value repeated.
doc: To store a cell array in a field, wrap it in another cell: `struct('a', {{1, 2}})`. `struct('a', {})` is an empty struct array with field a.

examples.expected:
s = 

  struct with fields:

    a: 1
    b: 'text'

differs: struct([]) is refused (MATLAB gives a 0-by-0 struct with no fields).
Converting an object to a structure (struct(obj)) is not supported.
